# Shared component patterns

Use these as API-shape examples, then adapt names and tokens to the target project. Extract a new primitive after two matching occurrences; fold a single occurrence into an existing primitive.

## Three-slot header

Use slots because each screen may supply different view kinds.

### SwiftUI

```swift
struct AppHeaderBarView<Leading: View, Center: View, Trailing: View>: View {
    let leading: Leading
    let center: Center
    let trailing: Trailing

    init(
        @ViewBuilder leading: () -> Leading,
        @ViewBuilder center: () -> Center,
        @ViewBuilder trailing: () -> Trailing
    ) {
        self.leading = leading()
        self.center = center()
        self.trailing = trailing()
    }

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: DesignTokens.headerSpacing) {
            leading
            Spacer()
            center
            Spacer()
            trailing
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, DesignTokens.screenPadding)
    }
}

AppHeaderBarView {
    Button(action: onBack) { Image(IconNames.back) }
} center: {
    Text(Localization.booking.localized)
} trailing: {
    Image(IconNames.notifications)
}
```

### Compose

```kotlin
@Composable
fun AppHeaderBar(
    leading: @Composable () -> Unit,
    center: @Composable () -> Unit,
    trailing: @Composable () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    Row(
        modifier = modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .padding(horizontal = CustomTheme.dimens.screenPadding),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
    ) {
        leading()
        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        center()
        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        trailing()
    }
}
```

## Primary action

The shared API owns common styling; callers supply localized text and behavior.

### SwiftUI

```swift
struct PrimaryActionButtonView: View {
    let title: String
    let action: () -> Void

    var body: some View {
        Button(title, action: action)
            .buttonStyle(PrimaryActionButtonStyle())
    }
}

PrimaryActionButtonView(
    title: Localization.bookNow.localized,
    action: viewModel.book
)
```

### Compose

```kotlin
@Composable
fun PrimaryActionButton(
    text: String,
    onClick: () -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
) {
    Button(
        onClick = onClick,
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
    ) {
        Text(
            text = text,
            style = CustomTheme.typography.button,
            color = CustomTheme.colors.onPrimary,
        )
    }
}

PrimaryActionButton(
    text = stringResource(R.string.book_now),
    onClick = onBook,
)
```

## Labeled field

Use one primitive for cases with the same decoration and interaction contract. Keep unlabeled search separate when its prompt, accessibility, or behavior differs.

### SwiftUI

```swift
struct LabeledTextFieldView: View {
    let label: String
    let placeholder: String
    @Binding var text: String
    var leading: Image?
    var trailing: Image?

    var body: some View {
        VStack(
            alignment: .leading,
            spacing: DesignTokens.fieldLabelSpacing
        ) {
            Text(label)
            HStack(spacing: DesignTokens.fieldContentSpacing) {
                if let leading {
                    leading.accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                TextField(placeholder, text: $text)
                if let trailing {
                    trailing.accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .textFieldStyle(AppTextFieldStyle())
        }
    }
}

LabeledTextFieldView(
    label: Localization.destination.localized,
    placeholder: Localization.chooseDestination.localized,
    text: $viewModel.destination,
    trailing: Image(IconNames.search)
)
```

### Compose

```kotlin
@Composable
fun LabeledTextField(
    label: String,
    value: String,
    onValueChange: (String) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    leading: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
    trailing: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null,
) {
    Column(
        modifier = modifier,
        verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(CustomTheme.dimens.fieldLabelSpacing),
    ) {
        Text(
            text = label,
            style = CustomTheme.typography.label,
            color = CustomTheme.colors.textSecondary,
        )
        OutlinedTextField(
            value = value,
            onValueChange = onValueChange,
            leadingIcon = leading,
            trailingIcon = trailing,
        )
    }
}
```

## Segmented selector

Use a typed option and one selected value.

### SwiftUI

```swift
struct SegmentedSelectorView<Option: Hashable>: View {
    let options: [Option]
    let title: (Option) -> String
    @Binding var selection: Option

    var body: some View {
        Picker("", selection: $selection) {
            ForEach(options, id: \.self) { option in
                Text(title(option)).tag(option)
            }
        }
        .pickerStyle(.segmented)
    }
}
```

### Compose

```kotlin
@Composable
fun <T> SegmentedSelector(
    options: List<T>,
    selected: T,
    label: (T) -> String,
    onSelect: (T) -> Unit,
) {
    Row {
        options.forEach { option ->
            FilterChip(
                selected = option == selected,
                onClick = { onSelect(option) },
                label = {
                    Text(
                        text = label(option),
                        style = CustomTheme.typography.label,
                        color = CustomTheme.colors.textPrimary,
                    )
                },
            )
        }
    }
}
```

## Choosing whether shapes match

Treat differences in text, icons, selected values, and optional slot content as parameters. Keep components separate when the underlying widget, interaction, accessibility contract, or rendered structure differs—for example, multi-line editing versus a single-line field.
